According to Mark Gurman's latest Power On newsletter, Apple is working to turn its upcoming non-augmented reality (AR) smart glasses into another health and fitness platform — though these features likely won't debut in the first-generation model launching next year.

Per his report, Apple had earlier sought to turn the Vision Pro into a health platform. The company was reportedly developing a version of its Fitness+ app for the headset, letting users watch workout videos, track their movements, and close their Activity rings on Apple's first spatial computing device.

There were also plans to include some special physical motion-tracking analytics to set it apart from devices like the iPad or Apple TV. However, due to the headset being too heavy, Apple ultimately abandoned those plans:

That said, the company is now revisiting similar ideas through its upcoming smart glasses — though the lack of a display will force some design adjustments.

Fitness on smart glasses

Apple's specific plans for smart glasses remain unclear, but it is hiring for these efforts. The report notes:

For me, the two obvious features are the Workout Buddy that launched on the Apple Watch last year, and potentially a built-in heart-rate sensor in the glasses (like the one that debuted in the AirPods Pro 3). That setup has a real chance of making the glasses a great companion for runners.

Cameras could also play a role across different activities, letting the system see whether users are performing movements correctly and helping them improve their workouts.

What Apple ultimately delivers remains to be seen. As noted at the top, these features likely won't appear in the first-generation model — meaning the full vision may not arrive for several more years.
